# dtcloud_volumes (Data Source)

Lists the volumes visible to the caller.

The list endpoint reports a flatter shape than the details one: the attached machine's name and
status are folded onto the volume, and the size arrives as text such as `"20 GB"`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "dtcloud_volumes" "all" {}

data "dtcloud_volumes" "on_web" {
  attached_to_id = dtcloud_vm.web.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `attached_to_id` (String) Only return volumes attached to this VM. Applied by the provider — the API has no filter.
- `name` (String) Only return volumes with this exact name. Applied by the provider — the API has no filter.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `volumes` (List of Object) The volumes that matched. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--volumes))

<a id="nestedatt--volumes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `volumes`

Read-Only:

- `attached_to` (String)
- `attached_to_id` (String)
- `attached_to_status` (String)
- `bootable` (Boolean)
- `id` (String)
- `is_detachable` (Boolean)
- `name` (String)
- `size` (Number)
- `status` (String)
- `storage_policy` (String)
- `volume_type` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

~> **The filters are applied by the provider, not the API.** The list route takes no query
parameters, so every read fetches every volume. The filters are a convenience, not a smaller request.

* **`size` is normalised** to a whole number of GB, so it means the same thing here, on
  `dtcloud_volume` and on the resource.
* **There is no image metadata and there are no timestamps here.** Read one volume with
  `dtcloud_volume` when you need them.
